title: A package with no protocol range installs with the compatibility check skipped, and only the server log says so
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

Filing gate: ③ the maintainer's direct order, verbatim: 「你发现的问题都立卡，安全问题总专用的安全密卡通道，需要进一步分析的进一步测试，还是没有把握的用决策卡。」 (2026-11-05). Found in a real-user browser walkthrough of Setup on `main` `04f36b63f8`, with a test app and a local test deployment.

**Business reason.** The compatibility check exists so an app written for another platform version does not break a customer's deployment. When it is skipped, the administrator clicking Install is the person who needs to know, and they do not read server logs.

**Reader.** The server lane dev for the install answer in `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, and the UI lane for showing it.

**Duplicates.** Searched `engines.protocol package marketplace warning admin` (19 hits). #21727, closed, is a different case: an incompatible package answered with a 500. The rest are QA run anchors.

## Measured

Installing HotCRM v6.0.0 from the marketplace, the server log says:

`WARN [MarketplaceInstallLocal] [protocol] package 'app.objectstack.hotcrm' declares no engines.protocol range; loading under protocol 18.0.0 without a compatibility check (ADR-0087).`

The page says only that the install succeeded. The detail page shows no platform version information.

## Expected

The install answer carries this, and the page shows it in plain words, for example that the app did not state which platform version it supports and was not checked for compatibility. Whether publishing should also warn or refuse such a package is a separate choice. If the dev finds it needs a contract change, report it rather than deciding in the PR.
